claim: The gastric proton pump (H+,K+-ATPase) is a P-type ATPase responsible for gastric acidification.
source: The gastric proton pump (H+,K+-ATPase), a P-type ATPase responsible for gastric acidification, mediates electro-neutral exchange of H+ and K+ coupled with ATP hydrolysis, but with an as yet undetermined transport stoichiometry.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of the enzyme.

claim: The gastric proton pump mediates electro-neutral exchange of H+ and K+ coupled with ATP hydrolysis.
source: The gastric proton pump (H+,K+-ATPase), a P-type ATPase responsible for gastric acidification, mediates electro-neutral exchange of H+ and K+ coupled with ATP hydrolysis, but with an as yet undetermined transport stoichiometry.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations throughout the manuscript (Sachs et al., 1976; van der Hijden et al., 1990; Burnay et al., 2001; Burnay et al., 2003).

claim: Crystal structures of the pump in the E2-P transition state were determined at a resolution of 2.5 Å.
source: Here we show crystal structures at a resolution of 2.5 Å of the pump in the E2-P transition state, in which the counter-transporting cation is occluded.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by crystallographic data in Table 1.

claim: A single K+ is bound to the cation-binding site of the H+,K+-ATPase in the E2-P transition state.
source: We found a single K+ bound to the cation-binding site of the H+,K+-ATPase, indicating an exchange of 1H+/1K+ per hydrolysis of one ATP molecule.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 3 and anomalous difference Fourier maps.

claim: The H+,K+-ATPase exchanges 1H+/1K+ per hydrolysis of one ATP molecule.
source: We found a single K+ bound to the cation-binding site of the H+,K+-ATPase, indicating an exchange of 1H+/1K+ per hydrolysis of one ATP molecule.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of a single K+ binding site and the electroneutrality of transport.

claim: The 1H+/1K+ exchange stoichiometry fulfills the energy requirement for the generation of a six pH unit gradient across the membrane.
source: This fulfills the energy requirement for the generation of a six pH unit gradient across the membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by thermodynamic calculations shown in Figure 1.

claim: The highly acidic environment (pH 1) in the stomach is generated by the gastric proton pump, H+,K+-ATPase.
source: The highly acidic environment (pH 1) in the stomach is generated by the gastric proton pump, H+,K+-ATPase, which mediates an exchange of H+ and K+ across the parietal cell membrane that is coupled with ATP hydrolysis (Figure 1) (Ganser and Forte, 1973).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to Ganser and Forte, 1973.

claim: The H+,K+-ATPase mediates an exchange of H+ and K+ across the parietal cell membrane that is coupled with ATP hydrolysis.
source: The highly acidic environment (pH 1) in the stomach is generated by the gastric proton pump, H+,K+-ATPase, which mediates an exchange of H+ and K+ across the parietal cell membrane that is coupled with ATP hydrolysis (Figure 1) (Ganser and Forte, 1973).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation.

claim: The vectorial cation transport of gastric H+,K+-ATPase is accomplished by cyclical conformational changes in the enzyme.
source: Like other P-type ATPases, the vectorial cation transport of gastric H+,K+-ATPase is accomplished by cyclical conformational changes in the enzyme (abbreviated as 'E') (Rabon and Reuben, 1990), generally described using E1/E2 nomenclature based on the Post-Albers scheme for Na+,K+-ATPase (Figure 2A) (Post et al., 1969).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to Rabon and Reuben, 1990 and Post et al., 1969.

claim: A conserved aspartate is reversibly auto-phosphorylated to form phosphoenzyme intermediates during the transport cycle.
source: During the transport cycle, a conserved aspartate is reversibly auto-phosphorylated to form phosphoenzyme intermediates (EPs), a hallmark of members of the P-type ATPase family (Post and Kume, 1973).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to Post and Kume, 1973.

claim: The H+,K+-ATPase consists of two subunits: a 110 kDa catalytic α-subunit and a β-subunit.
source: The H+,K+-ATPase consists of two subunits. The 110 kDa catalytic α-subunit is homologous to other related P2-type ATPases such as Na+,K+-ATPase, with which it shares 65% identity (Morth et al., 2007), and the serco(endo)plasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) (Toyoshima et al., 2000), with which it shares 35% sequence identity (Palmgren and Axelsen, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations.

claim: The catalytic α-subunit of H+,K+-ATPase shares 65% identity with Na+,K+-ATPase.
source: The 110 kDa catalytic α-subunit is homologous to other related P2-type ATPases such as Na+,K+-ATPase, with which it shares 65% identity (Morth et al., 2007), and the serco(endo)plasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) (Toyoshima et al., 2000), with which it shares 35% sequence identity (Palmgren and Axelsen, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to Morth et al., 2007.

claim: The catalytic α-subunit of H+,K+-ATPase shares 35% sequence identity with SERCA.
source: The 110 kDa catalytic α-subunit is homologous to other related P2-type ATPases such as Na+,K+-ATPase, with which it shares 65% identity (Morth et al., 2007), and the serco(endo)plasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) (Toyoshima et al., 2000), with which it shares 35% sequence identity (Palmgren and Axelsen, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to Toyoshima et al., 2000 and Palmgren and Axelsen, 1998.

claim: The α-subunit is composed of 10 transmembrane (TM) helices, in which the cation-binding sites are located.
source: The α-subunit is composed of 10 transmembrane (TM) helices, in which the cation-binding sites are located, and three cytoplasmic domains (the nucleotide (N), phosphorylation (P) and actuator (A) domains) that catalyze ATP hydrolysis and the auto-phosphorylation reaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a structural description.

claim: The α-subunit has three cytoplasmic domains (N, P, and A domains) that catalyze ATP hydrolysis and the auto-phosphorylation reaction.
source: The α-subunit is composed of 10 transmembrane (TM) helices, in which the cation-binding sites are located, and three cytoplasmic domains (the nucleotide (N), phosphorylation (P) and actuator (A) domains) that catalyze ATP hydrolysis and the auto-phosphorylation reaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a structural and functional description.

claim: The β-subunit is a single-span membrane protein with a short N-terminal cytoplasmic tail and a large C-terminal ectodomain.
source: The β-subunit is a single-span membrane protein with a short N-terminal cytoplasmic tail and a large C-terminal ectodomain, and it is involved in correct membrane integration and targeting of the complex to the cell surface (Chow and Forte, 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to Chow and Forte, 1995.

claim: The β-subunit is involved in correct membrane integration and targeting of the complex to the cell surface.
source: The β-subunit is a single-span membrane protein with a short N-terminal cytoplasmic tail and a large C-terminal ectodomain, and it is involved in correct membrane integration and targeting of the complex to the cell surface (Chow and Forte, 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to Chow and Forte, 1995.

claim: The free energy derived from ATP hydrolysis (ΔGATP) in the parietal cell is about −13 kcal/mol.
source: The free energy that is derived from ATP hydrolysis, ΔGATP—calculated from ΔG'0 and the measured intracellular concentrations of ATP, ADP and Pi in the parietal cell—is about −13 kcal/mol (Durbin et al., 1974).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1 caption with a citation to Durbin et al., 1974.

claim: Under physiological conditions in intact parietal cells with an internal pH of approximately 7, a pH gradient of at least 6 pH units must be created.
source: Under physiological conditions in intact parietal cells with an internal pH of approximately 7, a pH gradient of at least 6 pH units must be created.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1 caption.

claim: Taking reasonable values of pH 7 and 120 mM K+ for intracellular conditions and the measured pH (1.0) and K+ concentration (10 mM) of the gastric juice, concentration gradients across the parietal cell membrane are 10^6 and 12 times for H+ and K+, respectively.
source: Taking reasonable values of pH 7 and 120 mM K+ for intracellular conditions and the measured pH (1.0) and K+ concentration (10 mM) of the gastric juice, we can calculate concentration gradients across the parietal cell membrane of 106 and 12 times for H+ and K+, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1 caption and in the Introduction.

claim: For an electro-neutral H+/K+ exchange pump for which NH+=NK+=1, the sum of chemical potentials is about −10 kcal/mol.
source: For an electro-neutral H+/K+ exchange pump for which NH+=NKK+=1, the sum of chemical potentials is about −10 kcal/mol, and is within the range of ATP free energy (Reenstra and Forte, 1981).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1 caption with a citation to Reenstra and Forte, 1981.

claim: If the exchange of two cations is assumed (NH+=NK+=2), the reaction is thermodynamically disallowed at pH 1.
source: However, if the exchange of two cations is assumed, in which case NH+=NKK+=2, the reaction is thermodynamically disallowed at pH 1.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1 caption.

claim: The ratio of H+ transported to ATP hydrolyzed must be approximately 1, and cannot be as large as 2, when gastric pH is around 1.
source: Therefore, the ratio of H+ transported to ATP hydrolyzed must be approximately 1, and cannot be as large as 2, when gastric pH is around 1.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 1 caption and in the Introduction.

claim: A previous investigation of H+ transport shows a 1:1 stoichiometry of H+ transport and ATP hydrolysis at pH 6.1–6.9.
source: Accordingly, a previous investigation of H+ transport shows a 1:1 stoichiometry of H+ transport and ATP hydrolysis at pH 6.1–6.9 (Reenstra and Forte, 1981).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to Reenstra and Forte, 1981.

claim: A separate investigation showed the transport of two H+'s for each ATP hydrolyzed at pH 6.1.
source: A separate investigation, on the other hand, showed the transport of two H+'s for each ATP hydrolyzed at pH 6.1 (Rabon et al., 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with a citation to Rabon et al., 1982.

claim: The electroneutrality of the transport cycle of the H+,K+-ATPase over a wide pH range is indisputable based on electrophysiological studies.
source: The electroneutrality of the transport cycle of the H+,K+-ATPase over a wide pH range is indisputable based on the electrophysiological studies (Sachs et al., 1976; van der Hijden et al., 1990; Burnay et al., 2001; Burnay et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction with citations to multiple studies.

claim: The Tyr799Trp mutant shows its highest ATPase activity in the absence of K+ and the activity decreases with increasing K+ concentration.
source: To our surprise, however, the Tyr799Trp mutant shows its highest ATPase activity in the absence of K+ and the activity decreases with increasing K+ concentration, in marked contrast to the K+-dependent increase in ATPase activity of the wild-type enzyme (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The wild-type enzyme shows K+-dependent increase in ATPase activity.
source: To our surprise, however, the Tyr799Trp mutant shows its highest ATPase activity in the absence of K+ and the activity decreases with increasing K+ concentration, in marked contrast to the K+-dependent increase in ATPase activity of the wild-type enzyme (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The observed K+-independent ATPase activity of Tyr799Trp in the absence of K+ indicates that the luminal gate of this mutant is spontaneously closed.
source: The observed K+-independent ATPase activity of Tyr799Trp in the absence of K+ indicates that the luminal gate of this mutant is spontaneously closed, like those of the previously reported constitutively active mutants (Abe et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Abe et al., 2018.

claim: The thermal stability of Tyr799Trp is significantly higher in the presence of K+ and AlFx than in the presence of AlFx alone.
source: The thermal stability (Hattori et al., 2012) of Tyr799Trp is significantly higher in the presence of K+ and AlFx than in the presence of AlFx alone (Figure 2F), qualitatively indicating K+-occlusion in the Tyr799Trp mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Hattori et al., 2012 and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The K+-occluded E2-P transition state is the most stable conformation of all of the evaluated conditions for Tyr799Trp.
source: This K+-occluded E2-P transition state is the most stable conformation of all of the evaluated conditions for Tyr799Trp, whereas for the wild-type enzyme, inhibitor-bound and luminal-open E2BeF is the most stable condition (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: For the wild-type enzyme, inhibitor-bound and luminal-open E2BeF is the most stable condition.
source: This K+-occluded E2-P transition state is the most stable conformation of all of the evaluated conditions for Tyr799Trp, whereas for the wild-type enzyme, inhibitor-bound and luminal-open E2BeF is the most stable condition (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Tyr799Trp prefers the luminal-closed K+-occluded state, (K+)E2-P.
source: We therefore conclude that Tyr799Trp prefers the luminal-closed K+-occluded state, (K+)E2-P, and is thus suitable for the structural analysis of the K+-occluded form.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on thermal stability and ATPase activity data.

claim: The Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx structure was determined at 2.5 Å resolution.
source: As expected, the crystals were significantly improved when using the Tyr799Trp mutant, which provided a 2.5 Å resolution structure in the best case [Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx] (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 1.

claim: The overall structure of H+,K+-ATPase Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx is very close to the corresponding structure of Na+,K+-ATPase.
source: The overall structure of H+,K+-ATPase Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx (Figure 3A) is very close to the corresponding structure of Na+,K+-ATPase (Morth et al., 2007; Shinoda et al., 2009) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Only a single K+ is observed in the cation-binding site of H+,K+-ATPase, instead of two K+ ions occluded in the transmembrane cation-binding site of the Na+,K+-ATPase.
source: However, instead of having two K+ ions occluded in the transmembrane cation-binding site of the Na+,K+-ATPase, only a single K+ is observed in the cation-binding site of H+,K+-ATPase (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: The observed single K+-binding is confirmed by the anomalous difference Fourier maps of Y799W(Rb+)E2-MgFx.
source: The observed single K+-binding is confirmed by the anomalous difference Fourier maps of Y799W(Rb+)E2-MgFx (Figure 3B), Y799W(Rb+)E2-AlFx and Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), which unambiguously show a single strong peak at the cation binding site located between TM4, TM5 and TM6 in the middle section of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The presence of saturating concentrations of cation (400 mM KCl or RbCl) in the crystallization buffer ensures high occupancy of K+ at the cation-binding site.
source: The presence of saturating concentrations of cation (400 mM KCl or RbCl) in the crystallization buffer ensures high occupancy of K+ at the cation-binding site, although several other binding sites, presumably low-affinity and/or non-specific, were determined in the cytoplasmic domains (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The wild-type WT(Rb+)E2-MgFx structure was determined at 4.3 Å resolution.
source: To exclude the possibility that the observed single K+-binding results from an artifact of the Tyr799Trp mutation, we determined the wild-type WT(Rb+)E2-MgFx structure in the same conformation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), despite its limited resolution of 4.3 Å.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 1.

claim: The molecular conformation of the wild-type H+,K+-ATPase is essentially the same as that of the Tyr799Trp mutant.
source: We therefore conclude that the molecular conformation of the wild-type H+,K+-ATPase is essentially the same as that of the Tyr799Trp mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural comparison.

claim: At the cation-binding site of the wild-type, a single Rb+ anomalous peak is found at the position close to the bound K+ in Tyr799Trp, as well as at site II in Na+,K+-ATPase.
source: At the cation-binding site of the wild-type, a single Rb+ anomalous peak is found at the position close to the bound K+ in Tyr799Trp, as well as at site II in Na+,K+-ATPase (Morth et al., 2007; Shinoda et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: An anomalous signal is hardly seen at the position corresponding to the cation-binding site I in Na+,K+-ATPase in the wild-type structure.
source: An anomalous signal is hardly seen at the position corresponding to the cation-binding site I in Na+,K+-ATPase, even at the low contour level (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: A single K+-binding in H+,K+-ATPase is supported by a Hill coefficient for K+ of close to 1.0.
source: A single K+-binding in H+,K+-ATPase is also supported by a Hill coefficient for K+ of close to 1.0 (Figure 2B), in marked contrast to the Hill coefficient of 1.5 for the K+-dependence of Na+,K+-ATPase (Sweadner, 1985) in which two K+ ions are occluded at the cation-binding site.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Sweadner, 1985 and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Hill coefficient for K+-dependence of Na+,K+-ATPase is 1.5.
source: A single K+-binding in H+,K+-ATPase is also supported by a Hill coefficient for K+ of close to 1.0 (Figure 2B), in marked contrast to the Hill coefficient of 1.5 for the K+-dependence of Na+,K+-ATPase (Sweadner, 1985) in which two K+ ions are occluded at the cation-binding site.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Sweadner, 1985.

claim: Crystals were generated at the close to neutral pH of 6.5.
source: Crystals were generated at the close to neutral pH of 6.5, the condition also used for previous in vitro H+ transport measurements (Reenstra and Forte, 1981; Rabon et al., 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: A single bound K+ observed in the crystal structure strongly indicates that H+,K+-ATPase transports only one K+ ion at once, and therefore only one H+ in the opposite direction, for every ATP hydrolyzed at neutral pH.
source: A single bound K+ observed in the crystal structure therefore strongly indicates that H+,K+-ATPase transports only one K+ ion at once, and therefore only one H+ in the opposite direction, for every ATP hydrolyzed at neutral pH (Figure 1, Hypothesis 1) (Reenstra and Forte, 1981).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Reenstra and Forte, 1981.

claim: In the Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx state, the cation-binding site is tightly shielded from the luminal solution by an extensive hydrophobic cluster centered around Tyr799Trp at the luminal gate.
source: Unlike the previously reported Rb+-bound and luminal-open (SCH)E2BeFx structure of H+,K+-ATPase (Abe et al., 2018), in the Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx state, the cation-binding site is tightly shielded from the luminal solution by an extensive hydrophobic cluster centered around Tyr799Trp (Figure 3C) at the luminal gate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Abe et al., 2018 and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A hydrogen bond between the nitrogen of the Trp799 residue and main chain carbonyl oxygen of Leu811 (3.3 Å) provides for the positioning of a Trp rotamer suitable for hydrophobic interactions with its surroundings.
source: A hydrogen bond between the nitrogen of the Trp799 residue and main chain carbonyl oxygen of Leu811 (3.3 Å, Figure 3C, Figure 4A) provides for the positioning of a Trp rotamer suitable for hydrophobic interactions with its surroundings, and stabilizes its conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C and Figure 4A.

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations support the presence of a hydrogen bond between the nitrogen of the Trp799 residue and main chain carbonyl oxygen of Leu811.
source: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support the presence of this hydrogen bond, and also show that in the wild-type enzyme, the hydroxyl group of Tyr799 makes a similar hydrogen bond with the main chain carbonyl oxygen of Leu811 (3.0 Å, Figure 4B, Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B and Video 1.

claim: In the wild-type enzyme, the hydroxyl group of Tyr799 makes a similar hydrogen bond with the main chain carbonyl oxygen of Leu811 (3.0 Å).
source: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support the presence of this hydrogen bond, and also show that in the wild-type enzyme, the hydroxyl group of Tyr799 makes a similar hydrogen bond with the main chain carbonyl oxygen of Leu811 (3.0 Å, Figure 4B, Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4B and Video 1.

claim: The side chain of Tyr is smaller than that of Trp, and thus forms a weaker hydrophobic network with the surrounding residues.
source: However, the side chain of Tyr is smaller than that of Trp, and thus forms a weaker hydrophobic network with the surrounding residues.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The stability of the luminal gate conformation shows larger fluctuation of Tyr799 in the wild-type when compared to that in the Tyr799Trp mutant.
source: These differences are reflected in the stability of the luminal gate conformation in the MD simulations, as seen in the larger fluctuation of Tyr799 in the wild-type when compared to that in the Tyr799Trp mutant (Figure 4C, Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4C and Video 1.

claim: The Leu811Gly mutant in the background of Tyr799Trp shows weak K+-dependence in its ATPase activity.
source: Although the Leu811Pro mutant is inactive, probably because it is unfolded during expression (as evaluated by fluorescence size-exclusion chromatography), the Leu811Gly mutant in the background of Tyr799Trp shows weak K+-dependence in its ATPase activity (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The Tyr799Trp + Ile803Ser mutant (Y799W/I803S) shows a K+-dependent increase in its ATPase activity.
source: Hydrophilic serine substitution of the surrounding hydrophobic residues in the Try799Trp background does not significantly change the inverse K+-dependence profile of Tyr799Trp activity, except that the Tyr799Trp + Ile803Ser mutant (Y799W/I803S) shows a K+-dependent increase in its ATPase activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: In the background of Y799W/I803S, an additional third mutation (Leu809Ser, Cys813Ser or Ile816Ser) restores K+-dependent ATPase activity to a level approximating that of the wild-type enzyme.
source: In the background of Y799W/I803S, an additional third mutation (Leu809Ser, Cys813Ser or Ile816Ser) restores K+-dependent ATPase activity to a level approximating that of the wild-type enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Spontaneous gate closure of the Tyr799Trp mutant is caused by the hydrophobic interactions with its surroundings.
source: These data suggest that spontaneous gate closure of the Tyr799Trp mutant is caused by the hydrophobic interactions with its surroundings, and that these interactions are facilitated by the favorable rotamer position of Tyr799Trp guided by the hydrogen-bond between Trp799 and Leu811 main chain.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on mutational analysis.

claim: The driving force for the gate closure is essentially the same as that in the wild-type enzyme.
source: We therefore conclude that the luminal-closed molecular conformation that is spontaneously induced by the Try799Trp mutation is not an artifact, and that the driving force for the gate closure is essentially the same as that in the wild-type enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on mutational analysis.

claim: Gate closure brings the luminal portion of TM4 (TM4L) close to TM6, effectively capping the cation-binding site from the luminal side of the membrane.
source: Gate closure brings the luminal portion of TM4 (TM4L) close to TM6, effectively capping the cation-binding site from the luminal side of the membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The lateral shift of TM4L is coupled to the vertical movement of the TM1,2 helix bundle connected to the A domain, leading to the ~30° rotation of the A domain that induces dephosphorylation of the aspartylphosphate.
source: This lateral shift of TM4L is coupled to the vertical movement of the TM1,2 helix bundle connected to the A domain, leading to the ~30° rotation of the A domain that induces dephosphorylation of the aspartylphosphate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The molecular events required for the luminal gate closure have been extensively studied in SERCA.
source: The molecular events required for the luminal gate closure have been extensively studied in SERCA (Olesen et al., 2004; Toyoshima et al., 2007; Toyoshima, 2009), and the same mechanism is observed in the H+,K+-ATPase, confirming the low-resolution maps of electron crystallography (Abe et al., 2011; Abe et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: The bound single K+ in H+,K+-ATPase is located at a position corresponding to site II of the Na+,K+-ATPase (2K+)E2-MgFx state.
source: The bound single K+ in H+,K+-ATPase is located at a position corresponding to site II of the Na+,K+-ATPase (2K+)E2-MgFx state (Morth et al., 2007; Shinoda et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: The bound K+ is coordinated by eight oxygen atoms located within 4 Å.
source: The bound K+ is coordinated by eight oxygen atoms located within 4 Å (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Table 2.

claim: Five oxygen atoms make a large contribution to K+ coordination (within 3 Å); they include three oxygen atoms from main-chain carbonyls (Val338, Ala339 and Val341) and two from side-chain carboxyl groups (Glu343 and Glu795).
source: Of these, five make a large contribution to K+ coordination (within 3 Å); they include three oxygen atoms from main-chain carbonyls (Val338, Ala339 and Val341) and two from side-chain carboxyl groups (Glu343 and Glu795).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The total valence for the bound K+ is 1.05 (optimal valence for K+ is 1.00).
source: The total valence (Kanai et al., 2013; Brown and Wu, 1976) for the bound K+ is 1.05 (optimal valence for K+ is 1.00), indicating that the K+ is almost ideally coordinated by the surrounding oxygen atoms (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and shown in Table 2.

claim: The valence for Rb+ coordination in the Y799W(Rb+)E2-MgFx structure is 1.14.
source: Similar results were obtained for Rb+ coordination in the Y799W(Rb+)E2-MgFx (valence 1.14) and Y799W(Rb+)E2-AlFx (valence 1.07) structures, but these results are clearly different from those previously reported for the Rb+-bound (SCH)E2BeFx structure (Abe et al., 2018) (valence 0.39, see Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Table 2.

claim: The valence for Rb+ coordination in the Y799W(Rb+)E2-AlFx structure is 1.07.
source: Similar results were obtained for Rb+ coordination in the Y799W(Rb+)E2-MgFx (valence 1.14) and Y799W(Rb+)E2-AlFx (valence 1.07) structures, but these results are clearly different from those previously reported for the Rb+-bound (SCH)E2BeFx structure (Abe et al., 2018) (valence 0.39, see Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Table 2.

claim: The valence for Rb+ coordination in the Rb+-bound (SCH)E2BeFx structure is 0.39.
source: Similar results were obtained for Rb+ coordination in the Y799W(Rb+)E2-MgFx (valence 1.14) and Y799W(Rb+)E2-AlFx (valence 1.07) structures, but these results are clearly different from those previously reported for the Rb+-bound (SCH)E2BeFx structure (Abe et al., 2018) (valence 0.39, see Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Abe et al., 2018 and shown in Table 2.

claim: As the TM4 helix is unwound at Pro342, coordination by the main chain carbonyl groups becomes possible.
source: As the TM4 helix is unwound at Pro342, coordination by the main chain carbonyl groups becomes possible (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Unwinding of TM4 provides a negative dipole moment (δ–) at the K+ site, which is located on the extension of TM4L at the helix breaking point.
source: Unwinding of TM4 also provides a negative dipole moment (δ–) at the K+ site, which is located on the extension of TM4L at the helix breaking point.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The short distance between the Glu343 carboxyl and Val341 carbonyl (2.6 Å) suggests protonation of Glu343.
source: The short distance between the Glu343 carboxyl and Val341 carbonyl (2.6 Å) suggests protonation of Glu343.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The juxtaposition of Glu795 and Glu820 indicates that at least one of the carboxyls must be protonated.
source: The juxtaposition of Glu795 and Glu820 indicates that at least one of the carboxyls must be protonated (Abe et al., 2018; Clement et al., 1970).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: The almost identical K+-affinity of the wild-type enzyme and the charge-neutralized mutant Glu795Gln suggests that the Glu795 carbonyl is protonated.
source: The almost identical K+-affinity of the wild-type enzyme and the charge-neutralized mutant Glu795Gln suggests that the Glu795 carbonyl is protonated (Abe et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Abe et al., 2018.

claim: The relatively distant location of Glu820 from the bound K+ is due to a salt bridge with Lys791.
source: The relatively distant location of Glu820 from the bound K+ is due to a salt bridge with Lys791.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: K+ is not trapped by the negative charge in the cation-binding site in spite of the crowded space and being surrounded by three glutamate residues.
source: Thus, K+ is not trapped by the negative charge in the cation-binding site in spite of the crowded space and being surrounded by three glutamate residues.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Oxygen atoms derived from either main chain carbonyl or protonated (Glu343 and Glu795) or charge-neutralized (Glu820) acidic side chains in the cation-binding site coordinate K+ through their lone-pair electrons.
source: Like water molecules, oxygen atoms derived from either main chain carbonyl or protonated (Glu343 and Glu795) or charge-neutralized (Glu820) acidic side chains in the cation-binding site coordinate K+through their lone-pair electrons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: This K+-coordination mode is consistent with the previously suggested K+-coordination mode in Na+,K+-ATPase.
source: This idea is consistent with the previously suggested K+-coordination mode in Na+,K+-ATPase (Yu et al., 2011; Rui et al., 2016; Cornelius et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: Qualitative estimation of pKa value using PROPKA suggests deprotonation of Asp824 (pKa = 5.4) and protonation of Glu936 (pKa = 10.8) in the crystal structure.
source: Indeed, qualitative estimation of pKa value using PROPKA (Li et al., 2005; Olsson et al., 2011; Søndergaard et al., 2011) suggests deprotonation of Asp824 (pKa = 5.4) and protonation of Glu936 (pKa = 10.8) in the crystal structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: The pKa of Asp942 is 7.6 in the crystal structure, but it drops to 5.4 ± 0.02, 4.8 ± 0.02 and 5.4 ± 0.02 in the last 50 ns of three runs of the Tyr799Trp MD simulation.
source: Although the pKa of Asp942 is 7.6 in the crystal structure, it drops to 5.4 ± 0.02, 4.8 ± 0.02 and 5.4 ± 0.02 in the last 50 ns of three runs of the Tyr799Trp MD simulation, supporting the idea that this residue can be considered to be deprotonated.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The protonation state expected from the crystal structure, namely, protonated Glu343, Glu795 and Glu936 (E343p/E795p/E936p) has a mean valence for K+ closest to the ideal value (1.07) in all examined simulation set-ups.
source: The calculated average valence from each 50 ns (latter half of 100 ns simulation)×3 copies of MD trajectories indicates that the protonation state expected from the crystal structure, namely, protonated Glu343, Glu795 and Glu936 (Figure 6, for E343p/E795p/E936p) has a mean valence for K+ closest to the ideal value (1.07) in all examined simulation set-ups (Table 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Table 3.

claim: During the simulation, K+ was stably coordinated at the cation-binding site, and the root mean squared deviation (RMSD) of the ion remained below 1.0 Å in the probable protonation states.
source: During the simulation, K+ was stably coordinated at the cation-binding site, and the root mean squared deviation (RMSD) of the ion remained below 1.0 Å in the probable protonation states.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The calculated pKa values for Glu343, Glu795 and Glu820 in the static crystal structure are 8.5, 11.1 and 10.8, respectively.
source: The calculated pKa values for Glu343, Glu795 and Glu820 in the static crystal structure are 8.5, 11.1 and 10.8, respectively, suggesting that the protonation status of E343p/E795p/E936p expected from the Tyr799Trp crystal structure is the most likely.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The salt bridge between Lys791 and Glu820 is a key feature of the cation-binding site of the H+,K+-ATPase (K+)E2-P state.
source: The salt bridge between Lys791 and Glu820 is a key feature of the cation-binding site of the H+,K+-ATPase (K+)E2-P state.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: RDF plots of Lys791 in E343p/E795p/E936p and E795p/E936p show sharp distributions with Glu820, indicating the formation of stable salt bridges between them during simulations.
source: RDF plots of Lys791 in E343p/E795p/E936p and E795p/E936p show sharp distributions with Glu820 (indicating the formation of stable salt bridges between them during simulations), which contrast markedly with the distribution predicted when a protonated Glu820 is assumed.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The cation-binding site structure of the wild-type enzyme is very similar to that of the Tyr799Trp mutant.
source: RDFs between the K+ ion and the coordinating oxygen atoms (Figure 6E–F) show that the ion coordination geometry of the wild-type is very similar to that of the mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6E-F.

claim: The RMSD of the ion-binding residues from the initial crystal structure is nearly identical for the wild-type enzyme and the Tyr799Trp mutant, indicating a stable coordination geometry in both systems.
source: Furthermore, the RMSD of the ion-binding residues (Figure 6I–J) from the initial crystal structure is nearly identical for the wild-type enzyme and the Tyr799Trp mutant, indicating a stable coordination geometry in both systems.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6I-J.

claim: In the K+-occluded E2-P transition state, a single K+ is observed at the cation-binding site of both the wild-type enzyme and the Tyr799Trp mutant.
source: In the K+-occluded E2-P transition state, a single K+ is observed at the cation-binding site of both the wild-type enzyme and the Tyr799Trp mutant (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Assuming electroneutral transport, one H+ must be exported in the prior luminal-open E2P state.
source: Assuming electroneutral transport (Sachs et al., 1976; van der Hijden et al., 1990; Burnay et al., 2001; Burnay et al., 2003), one H+ must be exported in the prior luminal-open E2P state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Extensive hydrogen bonds and a salt-bridge network centered on Glu820 in the luminal-open E2P state ensure that only one H+ is likely to be extruded from Glu820, regardless of the luminal pH.
source: Extensive hydrogen bonds and a salt-bridge network centered on Glu820 in the luminal-open E2P state ensure that only one H+ is likely to be extruded from Glu820, regardless of the luminal pH (Abe et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Abe et al., 2018.

claim: Even when the luminal solution is at neutral pH, one H+ will remain bound to Glu343.
source: Accordingly, even when the luminal solution is at neutral pH, one H+ will remain bound to Glu343, as suggested by the crystal structures (Figure 5) and supported by the MD simulations (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 5 and Figure 6.

claim: In the cation-binding site of the H+,K+-ATPase structure, there is not enough space to accommodate a second K+ at the position corresponding to site I of Na+,K+-ATPase.
source: In the cation-binding site of the H+,K+-ATPase structure, there is not enough space to accommodate a second K+ at the position corresponding to site I of Na+,K+-ATPase (Figure 5C,D, Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 5C,D and Figure 8.

claim: This restricted structure is due to the position of the Lys791 side chain and that of its salt-bridge partner Glu820.
source: This restricted structure is due to the position of the Lys791 side chain and that of its salt-bridge partner Glu820.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Lys791 and Glu820 are invariant for the gastric α1 isoform of H+,K+-ATPase, but are replaced with Ser782 and Asp811 (shark α1 sequence), respectively, in Na+,K+-ATPase.
source: These two amino acids are invariant for the gastric α1 isoform of H+,K+-ATPase, but are replaced with Ser782 and Asp811 (shark α1 sequence), respectively, in Na+,K+-ATPase (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ser782 in Na+,K+-ATPase plays an important role in K+-accommodation at site I.
source: In particular, Ser782 in Na+,K+-ATPase plays an important role in K+-accommodation at site I (Morth et al., 2007; Shinoda et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Replacing Ser with the bulky and positively charged Lys791 in H+,K+-ATPase would prevent K+ binding at a site I position.
source: Replacing Ser with the bulky and positively charged Lys791 in H+,K+-ATPase would prevent K+ binding at a site I position.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: When the two structures (H+,K+-ATPase and Na+,K+-ATPase) were superimposed, K+ at site I and a coordinating water molecule in Na+,K+-ATPase sterically clashed with the H+,K+-ATPase Lys791 side chain.
source: In fact, when the two structures (H+,K+-ATPase and Na+,K+-ATPase) were superimposed, K+ at site I and a coordinating water molecule in Na+,K+-ATPase sterically clashed with the H+,K+-ATPase Lys791 side chain (Figure 7), the position of which is defined by its salt-bridge partner Glu820 and by a hydrogen bond with the main chain carbonyl of Thr788 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 7 and Figure 5.

claim: The single K+ binding structure of H+,K+-ATPase represents a remarkable example of how energetic barriers faced by membrane pumps are overcome in living systems.
source: The single K+ binding structure of H+,K+-ATPase therefore represents a remarkable example of how energetic barriers faced by membrane pumps are overcome in living systems.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Evolutionary pressure selected single H+/K+ transport, rather than the more efficient double transport mode of 2H+/2K+, in order to achieve the thermodynamically challenging task of H+ uptake against a pH 1 solution in the stomach.
source: Evolutionary pressure selected single H+/K+ transport, rather than the more efficient double transport mode of 2H+/2K+, in order to achieve the thermodynamically challenging task of H+ uptake against a pH 1 solution in the stomach.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The wild-type H+,K+-ATPase or a Tyr799Trp mutant of the H+,K+-ATPase αβ-complex was expressed in the plasma membrane using baculovirus-mediated transduction of mammalian HEK293S GnT1– cells.
source: Briefly, the wild-type H+,K+-ATPase (WT) or a Tyr799Trp (Y799W) mutant of the H+,K+-ATPase αβ-complex was expressed in the plasma membrane using baculovirus-mediated transduction of mammalian HEK293S GnT1– cells purchased from ATCC (Goehring et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: The structure of Y799W(Rb+)E2-AlFx was determined by molecular replacement with PHASER, using an atomic model of H+,K+-ATPase in the SCH28080-bound E2BeF state (pdb ID: 5YLV) as a search model.
source: The structure of Y799W(Rb+)E2-AlFx was determined by molecular replacement with PHASER, using an atomic model of H+,K+-ATPase in the SCH28080-bound E2BeF state (pdb ID: 5YLV) as a search model.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Rubidium and potassium ions were identified in anomalous difference Fourier maps calculated using data collected at wavelengths of 0.8147 Å and 1.700 Å, respectively.
source: Rubidium and potassium ions were identified in anomalous difference Fourier maps calculated using data collected at wavelengths of 0.8147 Å and 1.700 Å, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx model contained 98.2/1.8/0.0% in the favored, allowed, and outlier regions of the Ramachandran plot, respectively.
source: The Y799W(K+)E2-MgFx, Y799W(Rb+)E2-MgFx, Y799W(Rb+)E2-AlFx and WT(Rb+)E2-MgFx models contained 98.2/1.8/0.0%, 98.3/1.7/0.0%, 98.2/1.8/0.0% and 91.1/8.8/0.1% in the favored, allowed, and outlier regions of the Ramachandran plot, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: All simulations were performed using GROMACS (v-2016.3).
source: All simulations were performed using GROMACS (v-2016.3) (Abraham et al., 2015; Berendsen et al., 1995; Hess et al., 2008; Pronk et al., 2013; Van Der Spoel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations.

claim: The CHARMM36 force field (v-July 2017) was used to model all the components of the system.
source: The CHARMM36 force field (v-July 2017) (Bjelkmar et al., 2010; Klauda et al., 2010; MacKerell et al., 1998; Mackerell et al., 2004) was used to model all the components of the system.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with citations.
